text: |-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Star Necklaces are Accessories in . The common variant can be purchased from the Korresia's Shop. The legendary variant can be obtained from Barbed Merod. The Moon Necklace is a direct upgrade to this accessory.
The Star Sand is an Important Item in . It is collected in the South Silent Sandsea in Sylvalum during the course of Star Sand Seeker.

|-|Real Mode= |-|Imaginary Mode= Star Strike (Japanese: , Puchimeteo, lit. "Petit Meteor") is MOMO's Level I Blade Special in . When MOMO is in Imaginary Mode, this Special turns into Star Strike (Dark).

Summon Flare (Japanese: , Samon Furea) is one of Melia's summon arts in and . It grants a Strength Up buff to Melia and allies within 10 meters, raising their Strength by 20% for each active flare element. Discharging the flare element delivers an ether attack to multiple enemies, inflicting a Blaze debuff which deals additional damage equal to 40% of the initial attack every 2 seconds.

Summer Stars (Japanese: , Tsuyu no Ichibanboshi, First Star of the Rainy Season) are collectables in . They can be found on the Fallen Arm. According to their description, Shulk admired them when he named them and they are so tangy that they make someone laugh.

Supercharge is a buff in . Supercharge boosts the power of the next Battle Art used, much like Magnum Charge in or Power Charge in . However, for Arts that hit multiple times in succession, only the first hit will be boosted.

This page lists all the quests available in Tephra Cave. The list may be viewed in the order they become available or the order they appear in the Quest Log. For simplicity, this page does not list additional prerequisites such as NPCs being registered on the Affinity Chart or having a certain affinity link with one another. Terms and abbreviations are explained in the legend at the bottom of the page. |-|Availability Order= This table is divided into sections based on the point in the story at which they become available (if other prerequisites are met). Quests within each section are sorted by the Area Affinity required. |-|Quest Log Order=

The Telethia Research is a Key Item in . It can be found in the Telethia Laboratory in the High Entia Tomb, and is needed to complete Secret Research. This item appears in , but is not obtainable. It can be seen in Teelan's Laboratory. After Teelan's Laboratory is destroyed by Gael'gar, Melia runs inside the burning lab in an attempt to save Teelan's research, but is only able to recover the Telethia Research tome in time before the lab is destroyed.

The Telethia Bridge (Japanese: , Tereshia-bashi) is a location in . It is located on the second floor of Agniratha, just south of the Meyneth Statue, and consists of the body of a petrified Telethia, presumably killed many aeons ago. The Destructive Bors can be found to its south, and the Meditative Varla to the north. A fire Ether Gear containing Strength Up IV and Weapon Power IV crystals can also be found nearby.

The Balance of Power (Japanese: , Pawā Baransu) is a quest in . It can be received by Dakuku in the Nopon Camp on Valak Mountain with Dunban in the lead. By completing this quest, Dunban's fourth Skill Tree, Obstinance, will be unlocked.

The Planet's Guardian is a Global Nemesis mission in . It is a mission to defeat Telethia Plume in Noctilum's Divine Roost, and can be received from the Squad Missions menu at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. To accept the mission, the player must use a BLADE Medal. This mission appears twice a week on a regular schedule, and remains available for 1, 2 or 3 days or until Telethia Plume has been defeated. In North America and Europe, Telethia Plume arrives every Monday and Friday at one of three random times. Unlike normal squad missions, The Planet's Guardian cannot be accepted until Chapter 6 is completed.

The Theospiti Temple Ruins (Japanese: , Teosupisuti Shinden-ato) are a Location in . They are ruins located in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal. Herald was sealed here many years ago after losing control of her power and destroying the temple. Herald's Sealed Core Crystal can be obtained as a reward by offering items at the Altar of Sealing, found behind a cracked wall of the Theospiti Temple Ruins.

The Water City is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. It will only become available after visiting the Kingdom of Uraya for the first time. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Beguiling Charms", "Production Mastery" and "Fortitude" Field Skills. It rewards store contracts that unlock the following wares: * Bipedal Crab Chili in Tomi Fishmongers * Victory Smoothie in Café Savvy * Coralline Marimba in Soniarus Music * Wood-Carven Queen in Cmalaf Artwork
The Mysterious White Fog is a Standard Quest in . The info fragments needed for this quest are obtained by going to a ? in Erythia Sea and from City Residents in the upper northeast of the City.

The Three Sage Tabernacle (Japanese: , San Daikenja no Shiseijo) is a Secret Area in . It is located on Valak Mountain of the Black Mountains. It is the Giants ruin of Three Sage Summit, with a Relic at the back of the room. The passage that led deeper into the ruin is now blocked off by snow.

Thinking Makes It So is an Affinity Mission in . After completing this mission, all Hraesvelg Skells will gain the ability to enter Cruise Mode while flying and have access to two additional Arts, Wing Blade and Hunter's Blow.

The Torl Marrin (Japanese: , Torai Mārin) is a Quest-Exclusive Boss in . It is a member of the Marrin family, and is fought at level 50 on the Goldmouth Flight Deck at the Argentum Trade Guild during Powered-Up Poppi. It deals spike damage when enraged (under 50% health).

Torna's Womb (Japanese: , Īra no Tai, Ira's Womb) is a landmark in . It is located below the city of Auresco, and can be accessed through an elevator outside of the city's rear gate. The womb itself is a massive, circular chamber that displays an image of the Blade and Titan life cycles. It also contains sixteen green stasis chambers that hold incubating Blades within them. The womb of the Tornan Titan eventually becomes the Womb Center after the Titan's demise. The Tenax Ekidno is fought on the natural platform outside the womb during Azurda SOS.

Vang Star Wings (Japanese: , Vanpu no Hoshibane) are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Tempest Vangs in the Windy Cave on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, shaking them creates a illusion of a shooting star and the workings of them are unclear. Two are required for the reconstruction of Colony 6. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 6,800 Noponstones.

Unreliable Rezno (Japanese: , Rensei no Rezōna) is a quest exclusive Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Lexos family, and can be found at the middle island of the Great Makna Falls in Makna Forest during the day only (6 a.m. to 5 p.m.). after the quest Final Challenge of the Sage is accepted after the events at Mechonis Core (Chapter 17). It will only spawn if there is not torrid weather, which is signified by a shimmering distortion on the screen. It can drop the Ocean Elixir of Life needed for Replica Monado 2 and Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Url Crevasse (Japanese: , Uru no sakeme) is a location in . It is a somewhat hidden location on the upper level of Valak Mountain. It is south of the Hollow Bone. The path to the crevasse is on the same altitude (i.e., do not descend into the Chilkin Lair) as the landmark. The path is somewhat blocked by a large crystal. The North Star Gusion appears here during snowy weather at night. The Pure Ice Flower that is needed for The Most Transparent Thing is found here.

Vague Barbas (Japanese: , Mōmō no Marubasu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 46 with a group of Reef Nebulae on a small plateau southwest of the Befalgar Pedestal in Valak Mountain. It can drop the Snow Elements needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction. The Vague Barbas can be reached by starting at Zokhed Pass, heading north down the mountain, bearing east up the hill, then crossing the natural bridge to the southwest, and finally continuing south to an oval-shaped area southeast of Nagul Waterfall. Later the Vague Barbas can be simply reached from the Befalgar Pedestal heading south through the tunnel.

Valak Mountain Research (Japanese: , Varaku Yukiyama Tenbō Chōsa) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from a Nopon Researcher at the Nopon Camp on Valak Mountain. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.

Vanguard Cetos (Japanese: , Vangādo Burikio) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Ceto family, and can be found at level 59 around Mount M'gando at night. They can also be found at level 52-57 on and around an unnamed island far southeast of Slavebird Isle in Cauldros Waters. The island does not appear on any of the regional maps.

Unloading of Goods (Japanese: , Tsumioroshi no Tetsudai) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild by talking to Khulkhan on the right side of the Goldmouth Flight Deck, when the nation has at least 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Transport Mastery" and "Fleet of Foot" Field Skills.
Universe Flicker (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using Knives. This art recycles Mòrag's Twin Moonblade.

Uniquely Disadvantaged is a Time Attack challenge in . It can be received from Nopon Archsage. The challenge battle is located at Gondorl Cathedral on Prison Island, it is unlocked after reaching Prison Island during Chapter 17.

Heal Harmony is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Signifer class that sets a field granting a Regenerate effect, healing 50% of user's Healing Power to allies in the field every two seconds. This art is exclusive to Fiona, and is a variant of Heal Harmony.
The Valak Peak Camp (Japanese: , Varaku-san no Kyūsokuchi) is a Rest Spot in . It is located on Valak Mountain on the Black Mountains.

The Vatura Flak is a Boss in . It is a member of the Flak family, and is fought at level 2 at Vermilion Woods. It is the first enemy fought by Matthew and A. It is both the only Flak and the only Origin-originating creature fought in , and the only one fought outside of Origin. Vatura Flaks are also seen aiding N in destroying the first City and killing its inhabitants, but are not fought.

The Wall Power Control Room (Japanese: , Bōheki Denryoku Kanrishitsu) is a location in . It is located on the Streets of the Land of Morytha, between the Wastes of Hubris and 7th Division. It is a small room surrounded by Guldo, containing a Treasure Trove and a power switch.
Voruk Draiguls are Normal Enemies in . They are members of the Draigul family and can be found at level 47 at Prison Island on the Black Mountains when there isn't Red Lightning.

Volitaris (Japanese: , Fuyū Tairiku, lit. Floating Continent) is the story-exclusive final region in . It is the mothership of Void and the Ganglion. It is a continent that floats above Mira. It is only accessible during Chapter 13 (Act 3). Unlike other regions, Volitaris has no FrontierNav Sites to install Data Probes at, due to FrontierNav being offline. There are also no collectibles, but there are purple collectible-like artifacts scattered around Volitaris that replenish 500 Skell Fuel each when collected. Additionally, the mini-map doesn't display any part of the region.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Whip Attachments (Japanese: , Sāberu Atatchimento) are accessories in . They increase the attack power of Whipsword-class weapons by up to 29%. This boosts their Auto-Attack stat during combat, increasing all damage dealt while using them. This attack power increase can stack with the effects of the Master Attachment accessory.

Xanadu Overlook (Japanese: , Mahoroba no Itadaki) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, at the eastern end of the mountain range north of Lake Ciel. It can be reached by following a mountain path from either FN Site 413 or Badr Stonebridge. Bobora can be found here during Castle in the Sky. As with all Scenic Viewpoints, its discovery yields an achievement ("Overlooking Xanadu Overlook").

Yachik is an NPC in . He is a humanoid male Common Blade who grants power to his Driver, Jac, with whom he is always found in particular in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain. Yachik wields a Megalance. He has a serious temperament and is unflinchingly loyal to his master, respecting his kindness but disappointed by his inability to stomach violence.

Xataris Spring (Japanese: , Zatarisu no Izumi) is a location in . It is located on the Central Plain of Temperantia. It is found on the eastern side of the plain south of the Titan Weapon Remains. The spring is a pool of a toxic liquid secreted by the Titan. In the middle of the pool is a flowery island. When the island is approached, Ravenwing Skull will appear. At the back of the pool is a small rock beach. Prior to and during the quest A Real Challenge, the seals of Light, Thunder, Ice, and Darkness can be found on the beach. After breaking the seals, the wall will explode, revealing a cave and Thanatobeast Andraz. A Treasure Trove can be found at the back of the cave.

Woodworking (Japanese: , Mokuzai no Kakō) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Forestry" and "Superstrength" Field Skills.

Yatata is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who appears on the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild as part of Fleecyflossy's quiz during Powered-Up Poppi, alongside Kalukalu and Lulumu. Yatata is one of the incorrect options in the quiz.

Zokhed Pass (Japanese: , Zokkuheddo-tōge) is a landmark in . It is the first landmark discovered on Valak Mountain. It connects the mountain to Makna Forest. A group of four Nopon Merchants are found here, one of whom has a shop. Another gives four Monster Quests.

Artifice Aion is the most powerful of the Artifices in Xenoblade Chronicles 2, capable of destroying Alrest, and the final boss of the game.

City Traderpon is an in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. He runs the City Caravan in the Centrilo Parade.

Colony Liberated is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. It plays when rebooting Ferronis Hulks, as well when liberating a Colony by destroying their Flame Clock during these quests: * Colony 30 in The Kind Right Hand. * Colony Tau in . * Colony Gamma in Going Beyond Power. * Colony 11 in The Wrath of Ashera. * Colony Iota in Her Reasons. * Colony Mu in Transparent Dreams. * Colony 15 in Doing It My Way.
The conservative faction are a group of City citizens in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. They are a political faction which believes that the City should stay out of the war between Keves and Agnus entirely.

Dazil, Town of Burning Sands (called Desert City Dazil on the Revival disc, sometimes unofficially referred to as Dazil ~ City of Burning Sands) is Disc 1, Track 11 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack and track 12 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack Revival Disc -the first and the last-. It is one of the tracks playable in the Nortune jukebox, under the option 'The World'. It plays as the area music in Dazil (as well as in all cutscenes in this area).

Elru is a country that existed in Xenogears. It was destroyed several years before the events of the game. This also refers to the unnamed continent south-east of the world where the nation is located.

is a music track in Xenosaga: Pied Piper. It is the area music for the following locations: * The Cathedral Entrance and Cathedral Courtyard. * The Galaxy Federation Police Station during the counter-terrorism training mission sidequest. * Jacob Medical Imprinting while in virtual space. * Mikhail's trap (as well as minor cutscenes during it). * Klaus's mind. * The Detention Center. * The Archon Zone Outskirts. * Erich's mind. * The . Flight (called Soaring on the Revival disc and Xenogears Vinyl - SHINKAKU -) is Disc 2, Track 9 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack, Track 35 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack Revival Disc -the first and the last-, and Track 3 of the B-Side of the first disc of Xenogears Vinyl - SHINKAKU -. The track is one of the tracks playable in the Nortune jukebox, under the option 'A Theme'. The track was remixed along with Wings for the Xenogears 20th Anniversary Concert -The Beginning and the End- as Soaring - Wings. A vocal remix was made for CREID titled Spring Lullaby. Finally, A Gathering of Stars in the Night Sky is a more mellow version of this track. It plays as the battle music against Ac

The Founders are a group of seven people who established the present day City and are the first Ouroboros. Their statues are located in Memorial Hall in Xenoblade Chronicles 3 and play an integral role in Future Redeemed. The citizens of the present day City are directly descended from the Founders.

, as indicated by the icon.]] Fuel is a mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Each Skell has a finite amount of fuel which is consumed in and when flying. If a Skell runs out of fuel, it cannot use Skell Arts or fly until it is refuelled. Fuel is measured in fuel "units". In the Wii U version, fuel units are displayed to the nearest hundredth with a green bar on the right of the UI. In the , this gauge only displays whole numbers. Each Skell has a maximum number of fuel units it can store at once; this varies depending upon Skell frame, ranging from 6750 at the lowest end to 28800 at the highest end. Each Skell frame also has varying statistics for how much fuel is consumed or gained by certai
House Vandham is one of the City's Six Noble Houses, families made of the descendants of the Founders. Its current head is Monica Vandham, who is also the Elder of the City.

The Immigrant Fleet is a widespread political and religious organization in the Xenosaga series that claims ownership of the . As a political body, they claim sovereignty over star systems populated by their religious followers in opposition to the Galaxy Federation's governing. The two groups have been at odds for centuries.
The Intersection is an apocalyptic event in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. It is a universe-wide annihilation event that will destroy the worlds of Bionis and Alrest.
Jackal is an enemy in Xenogears. It appears on the Mountain Path and in the Blackmoon Forest.

Lake Turkana, also known as Lake Rudolf, is a lake where the inciting incident of the Xenosaga series took place. It is located in the country of Kenya, on the continent of Africa, on the planet Earth.

Li Garte Prison Information is a discussion in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. It can be received by gathering intel at Corne Island and Thurbin Island during The Castle Beckons, and is required to complete this story quest.
Lost Jerusalem may refer to: * Lost Jerusalem (XG) - the planet from Xenogears * Lost Jerusalem (XS) - the planet from Xenosaga ** Lost Jerusalem (cutscene) - the cutscene in Xenosaga Episode III

Memories Left Behind (Revival Version) is track 47 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack Revival Disc -the first and the last- and Track 4 of the A-Side of the second disc of Xenogears Vinyl - SHINKAKU -. It is a vocal remix of Unstealable Jewel. Mikumari is a boss in Xenosaga Episode II - Jenseits von Gut und Böse. It is one of 3 es that cannot be fought until the player has completed the sidequest. Mikumari, alongside Baal Zebul and Phobos Rigas are exclusive to the English version of the game and is not found in the original Japanese version. It starts combat using a powerful attack called "Creeping in the Dark", an Ice attack that can also inflict L Blind. It also has Good Deed: a heavy-hitting Aura attack, Between Heaven and Earth: a thunder attack that hits both mechs if they are in the same row and inflicts L Charge Down (draining 75 EC at the end of every turn), and Purge Filth: an extremely powerful fire/strike attack that i

Michtam, formerly known as Abraxas is a planet in the Xenosaga series. It is the fourth planet in the Michtam System. Many believers of Ormus view Michtam as the "birthplace of Ormus" or the "holy land" due to the Immigrant Fleet settling there after departing .

Mikhail's trap is an area in Xenosaga: Pied Piper. It is constructed by Mikhail in order to trap Voyager. Its design has the motif of the streets of an old East Asian city in . This area is also used to introduce party leader mechanics: can detect traps, can detect chests, can destroy rubble, and 's encounter rate is halved.

In the Into the Open Sky, Panpan will ask for food pouch items because he can't complete his flight training with his stomach empty. To complete this, the party must exchange pouch items in order to get points. Once 100 points are accumulated, Panpan will fly all the way to Gormott, in the Forgotten Waste, in an attempt to complete his training.
The Power Distribution Facility is a sub-area on Second Miltia in Xenosaga Episode II - Jenseits von Gut und Böse. It is the power plant of Second Miltia.
The Red Dragon is an ability in the Xenosaga series. Activation of said ability is held solely by U.R.T.V. number 666, Rubedo.

STARS OF TEARS (OUT TAKE) (called Stars of Tears (Out Take) on the Revival disc) is Disc 1, Track 2 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack and track 2 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack Revival Disc -the first and the last-. It was also included as track 10 on the album Colours of Light (a compilation of Mitsuda's vocal works). Aspiration is an instrumental remix of this track. A Japanese version was made for CREID, called Two Wings. This track does not play in any cutscenes, areas, battles or menus in Xenogears. It was intended to play during a staff credits sequence after the opening cutscene; however, this was cut because it was decided that this would make the opening sequence too long.

The Salvator Faction is a large, fringe political group of the Galaxy Federation in the Xenosaga series. It was founded by Dmitri Yuriev and is mainly composed of Designer Children, including many powerful members of the Federation government.
Strength Support is the Soulhacker obtained from Killhappy Brijaidor in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. It increases the strength of s issued by the user.

is a track in Xenosaga Episode III. It has not been released on any soundtrack or sound selection and not much is known about this track. It is based on an accompaniment line from . It plays in the following cutscenes: * Suou Uzuki is attacked by the 27-Series Asura after protecting Shion. * T-elos confronts the party on Michtam. * The Elsa's crew realises that Gnosis are destroying the star cluster after Mary Magdalene awakens.

is track 2 on the CREID album. It is a version of STARS OF TEARS (OUT TAKE) with Japanese vocals (although the lyrics are substantially different from STARS OF TEARS' Japanese lyrics as provided in the Xenogears Original Soundtrack booklet, and their meaning is correspondingly different from that of the original).

Ultra Diamond Spatha is a in Xenoblade Chronicles X. The Spatha Series consists of Ether-based Longswords, which are highly prized for their use in Ether and Hercules Blow builds, and the Ultra Diamond Spatha is the strongest in the series. It's generally in competition with the Bewitched Glaive: Receding Rust, which has to offer a much higher weapon attack power and Ultrafauna Slayer as a battle trait. The Ultra Diamond Spatha, on the other hand, offers Potential Boost and (which generally give a stronger boost to the strongest melee/TP attacks than can be achieved with a Receding Rust when Howling Soul is a factor), as well as better stability and proper generation from s. Obtaining an Ult

Wings is Disc 2, Track 10 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack and track 36 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack Revival Disc -the first and the last-. The track was remixed along with Flight for the Xenogears 20th Anniversary Concert -The Beginning and the End- as Soaring - Wings, the 18th track on the associated Blu-Ray disc. It is one of the tracks playable in the Nortune jukebox, under the option 'The World'. The melody at 0:28 is based on a motif from Faraway Promise. It plays as the area music in the world map when the party is using the Yggdrasil III to fly. It also plays in the cutscene when the Goliath Airship takes off.

__NOTOC__ is Track 2 on the Xenosaga THE ANIMATION Original Soundtrack. It plays during the opening sequence at the start of each episode. It also plays in Episode 12 when KOS-MOS and Kirsch destroy the transformed E.S. Simeon together. Shining Hope is a remix of this piece. The main melody of the piece is also used as a motif in the following tracks: * Mysterious World * KOS-MOS Activating * Life and Death * Desperate Situation * Urgent Departure * A Secret Volition * * Endless Battle * Blue Planet ~ Endless Journey * Arrival The jingle that plays during the title drop of each episode is a slowed-down version of the start of this track.

The Xenogears Suite is track 11 on the Cafe SQ album. It is a suite of tracks from Xenogears, arranged for piano: * Premonition (0:00 to 1:06) * Dark Daybreak (1:08 to 2:37) * STARS OF TEARS (OUT TAKE)/Aspiration (2:37 to 4:13) * Flight (4:13 to 5:33) * In a Prison of Peace and Regret (5:34 to 6:27) * Our Wounded Bodies Shall Advance Towards the Light/A Prayer for the Joy Man Desires (6:28 to 7:21) * Unstealable Jewel (7:21 to 8:36) * Where the Egg of Dreams Hatches/lost... Broken Shards (8:36 to 9:42) * Faraway Promise/SMALL TWO OF PIECES ~Broken Shards~ (9:42 to 10:49)
Zoar was a planet in the Xenosaga series. It was the planet where the Zoar Incident began, setting off a chain of events that led to the Miltian Conflict.

Zanza's disciples, also known as the Trinity, are a trio of powerful beings from Bionis. They are Zanza's servants chosen by him to carry out his goal of destroying all life on Bionis to prepare for its rebirth.

Butterfly City is a song featured in the Japanese release of Yakuza 4, serving as its opening theme. The song is written, composed and performed by [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeebra Zeebra] in collaboration with RYO the SKYWALKER, Mummy-D and [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_(singer) DOUBLE]. It was released on his EP of same name in March 17, 2010. It was later re-released as the 14th track on his album "Black World/White Heat" in November 7, 2012.
Dreams of the Big City, or Big City Dreamin in the Remaster, is Taiga Saejima's 8th substory in Yakuza 5.

The Drunken Footpad is a human Syndicate agent found in the Alterac Mountains. He is a convenient source of Southshore Stout for Horde players who need to bribe Henchman Valik.

The Druid of the Fang were a group of druids found in the Wailing Caverns. Once part of an order of noble druids, the group, led by Naralex, sought to use the Caverns' underground springs to restore the Barrens to the lush and fertile land that it once was, using the power of the Emerald Dream. Hamuul Runetotem referred to them as a cult. However, once connected to the Dream, the druid's vision somehow became a nightmare, and began to corrupt and transform the Caverns and its denizens. Naralex and his druids were transformed into the Druids of the Fang, and began seeking to remake that land to match their own, twisted dreams. They were eventually defeated by a group of adventurers.

Drolig Blastpipe is a goblin vendor of Season 4 items. He is located in the Scryer's Tier in Shattrath City.

Droffers and Son Salvage is a shop located in the Drag of Orgrimmar, run by Dran Droffers and his son Malton. They are known to salvage goods with the help of Horde adventurers. They recovered the Hinterlands Honey Ripple and the Shattered Necklace plus the missing gems, put together in the Necklace and Gem Salvage. They also sell some Tier 3 armor in the Black Market Auction House.

of the cult.]] The Druids of the Flame are a sect of druids founded by Archdruid Fandral Staghelm, who served Ragnaros the Firelord as his loyal majordomo. Thrall referred to them as members of the Twilight's Hammer, and Fandral claimed to answer to the Twilight Prophet. However, the new iteration of the druids is dedicated to the Primal Incarnate Fyrakk and the Primalists' vision of the world. These vile creatures have turned their backs on Elune's teachings, and twisted by the insane power of the fire, they desire nothing more than to bury everything in ash. They operate mainly in the Firelands and can be distinguished from other night elves by their scarred red skin and burning orange eye

__NOTOC__ Droha is a draenei shaman trainer found in the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, next to Elissa Dumas and Rukua, busy in some kind of conversation with them. It is unknown whether he survived the Burning of Teldrassil or not.

__NOTOC__ Drowned Gilnean Merchants are Gilnean worgen found on the Shattershore of the Blasted Lands.
__NOTOC__ Drowned Gilnean Sailors are Gilnean worgen found on the Shattershore of the Blasted Lands.
__NOTOC__ Drowned Gilnean Settlers are Gilnean worgen found on the Shattershore of the Blasted Lands.
Dron Skyborn is an tauren flight master located around the Iron Docks in Gorgrond.

The Druids of the Fin are a group of druids who turn into sea lions. A group of them watches over the Emerald Bay in Val'sharah, but were put to sleep in shark-infested waters during one of their patrols by malevolent forest sprite tricksters. They were roused by order champions who also slew the sprites and destroyed the hypnotic water lilies.

Drum Circle is a Legion quest achievement that is rewarded for participating in a drum circle at the Thunder Drum in Highmountain. Five players must simultaneously jump up and down on the big center drum.
Drugon the Frostblood is an ettin who can be found in Highmountain.
Druids of the Moon are night elves located in the Temple of Elune of Val'sharah. They are being tended to by the Temple Priestesses. They are also seen in Deliverance Point on the Broken Shore.
Drudge Supervisors are gnomes found on Alcaz Island in Dustwallow Marsh.
The Drogbar Stash can be found behind Gelmogg in the Lifespring Cavern in Highmountain

The Drowned Thistleleaf is a bait item that can be fished up from open water in Val'sharah and from Mossgill Perch Schools, with an increased chance to be caught when using an Arcane Lure. It is also sold by Keeper Raynae for . When this item is used, the angler is provided a buff (Blessing of the Thistleleaf) which provides a higher chance to catch Thorned Flounder for two minutes. If this item is used after having obtained the Underlight Angler, one will instead be able to catch Thorned Flounder (artifact power).
Drogbar Manathirsters are drogbar located in Lifespring Cavern in Highmountain. They summon Blistering Geodes.
Drogbar Rivertrollers are drogbar located in Whitewater Wash in Highmountain.
Drogbar Wormhooks are drogbar located in Whitewater Wash in Highmountain.
Drogbar Trader is a vision of a drogbar located in Highmountain. He appears upon interacting with the Ancient Spirit Drum.
Drooble is an Alterac brewhound located in Redridge Pass in Redridge Mountains during Tracking Tipoff. If Hunter McAlister‎ is killed first, Drooble runs away.
Drums of Primal Might are crafted with Leatherworking, and imbued with Elune's power by Daniss Ghostdancer. The recipe is only available during the quest.

__NOTOC__ Droman Krelnor is a vorkai located in Ardenweald. He was the droman master of Heartswood Grove and the Shrouded Mire. Krelnor is first seen receiving Featherlight's message from the Winter Queen tells which wildseeds were to be saved and moved to Tirna Vaal. Later, when the grove was attacked by the possessed fae and Drust, he becomes one of the possessed and steals Heartswood Grove's heart. He is confronted and defeated by an alliance of Te'zan, Niya, Warden Casad, and an adventurer. Upon his death, he apologizes to Niya as the heart crumbles to ash from the Drust's magic.

Droman Aliothe is a Wild God located at Hibernal Hollow in Ardenweald. In life, she lived on an unknown world. When the Burning Legion attacked her world, she died, and it was destroyed. She was sent to Ardenweald in the afterlife, where she is now a Droman of the Court of Night.
Dripping Fang is an anima power for tanks and DPS. It can be chosen after defeating Soggodon the Breaker in Mythic+ dungeons with the Tormented affix.
Droplets are oozes that can be encountered during Island Expeditions.
Drugon's Snowglobe drops from Drugon the Frostblood in Highmountain.

Dun Algaz (or Algaz Gate) is the tunneled mountain pass area between Loch Modan and the Wetlands, as well as the name of a stronghold located in the pass. It is bordered by Algaz Station in Loch Modan and Slabchisel's Survey in the Wetlands.

Drywhisker Gorge is a gorge cutting through the mountains in the eastern section the Arathi Highlands, northeast of Hammerfall. At the end of the gorge lies a cave. It is currently inhabited by the Drywhisker kobolds. Deep within the cave, a mysterious stone shard can be found in which a piece of the essence of Princess Myzrael was trapped. These kobolds, allies to the giants, guard the motes and the shard within. By the time of the Battle for Stromgarde, the Drywhisker kobolds still remained active in this area. The Dry Hills are located in the far northwestern corner of the Northern Barrens. Despite their name, the Dry Hills are actually one of the greener areas of the Barrens because the seeds from the nearby Ashenvale Forest have been carried on the wind over the crags. These foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains to the west are primarily populated by Witchwing harpies who have recently been raiding caravans traveling the northern Gold Road. However, the large number of zhevra, plainstriders, raptors, and other animals in this area has drawn many hunters here. During the Primalists' attack, the area was invaded by elementals. Their presence imbued the harpies.

Duhng is an orc cooking trainer located in a hut just east of the Crossroads, at the foot of a mountain, in the Northern Barrens. During the Legion Invasions, he was cowering in fear behind Guard Taruc.

Duncan Senturus was a paladin of the Silver Hand towards the end of the Second War. He was the son of a wealthy lord. The gray-bearded paladin and a detachment of his men encountered Rhonin — on a mission by the Kirin Tor to travel to Khaz Modan — and Vereesa Windrunner as they made their way to the port of Hasic. Though Duncan (and indeed, most paladins) were distrustful of "wizards", his bias was tempered somewhat by Vereesa. After discovering that Hasic had been almost completely destroyed, Rhonin, Vereesa, and Duncan were forced to join up with Falstad Dragonreaver and his wing of gryphon riders in order for Rhonin to reach Khaz Modan. While en route, they were ambushed by Dragonmaw drag
Dune Smashers were mountain giants located in the Valley of the Watchers in southern Tanaris.

Dun Baldar Pass is a passage located in the northern area of Alterac Valley. It runs south from the Alliance entrance to the valley, then it reaches a lumber mill, and finally goes west into a crossroads between Dun Baldar and Icewing Bunker. It is always guarded by Stormpike Guards. The Horde counterpart is called Frostwolf Pass. Dun Baldar Pass is in a mountainous area and is relatively close to the Stormpike Graveyard. However, the graveyard is at the bottom of a cliff, so the short way to get there would require taking fall damage.

Dun Baldar South Bunker is the bunker located in the southeastern part of Dun Baldar. Like all alliance bunkers in Alterac Valley, it is guarded by archers with relatively weak melee attack ability. The Alliance Wing Commanders, if rescued, stand just west of this bunker. In addition, there are trade, general goods, and food vendors in a tent just northwest of its entrance.
__NOTOC__ Du'ga is a jungle troll flight master located at Zabra'jin in Zangarmarsh.

Dun Garok Mountaineers are dwarves patrolling outside Dun Garok in Hillsbrad Foothills.

Dun Argath is the second mission of the Horde campaign in Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness Shareware. This is an early version of the mission Southshore as seen in the retail game. It shares similar mission objectives, but the map design and mission briefing are different: in the retail game the Horde chooses to attack the kingdom of Lordaeron through the island of Zul'Dare rather than through Khaz Modan. In the retail game the Horde does not turn towards Khaz Modan until the second act.

Dual Talent Specialization (or dual spec) was a skill available to learn at level 30 from class trainers for . Introduced in patch 3.1.0, dual talent specialization was the ability to create and switch between two distinct 'specs'. Each spec comprises a specialization and a full set of talents, glyphs, and action bars. It was an economical alternative to resetting all of these if the player intended to switch between the same two specs frequently, or simply allowing the player to experiment more freely and cheaply. In World of Warcraft: Legion players can now switch between all of their specs rather than being limited to just two, and no longer requires gold to activate the option.

The Drywhiskers are a group of kobolds found in the Arathi Highlands. They're allied with the mountain giants Fozruk and Thenan who trapped Myzrael deep beneath the Arathi Highlands. They have Iridescent Shards, shards like Shards of Myzrael, deep within the cave in their Drywhisker Gorge. By the time of the Battle for Stromgarde, the Drywhisker kobolds still remained active in this region. Among them, Geomancer Flintdagger and Overseer Krix were priority targets. Krix eventually succumbed to his opponents, and the Lil' Donkey that was to be his dinner was saved and found a new home. The Drysnap is a tribe of makrura found near the coastline of Desolace. They pulled the first mate of Ulysses Rackmore, captain of the Gallant, into the deeps of the ocean. The Slitherblade naga seem to be at war with them. They have a tendency to get trapped in the Shellfish Trap.
The Dun Baldar North Marshal guards Vanndar Stormpike in the fortress of Dun Baldar in Alterac Valley until the Dun Baldar North Bunker is destroyed.
The Dun Baldar South Marshal guards Vanndar Stormpike in the fortress of Dun Baldar in Alterac Valley until the Dun Baldar South Bunker is destroyed.
The Dun Baldar North Warmaster guarded Drek'Thar in Frostwolf Keep in Alterac Valley after the Dun Baldar North Bunker was destroyed.
The Dun Baldar South Warmaster guarded Drek'Thar in Frostwolf Keep in Alterac Valley after the Dun Baldar South Bunker was destroyed.

Dun Morogh is a level 1-20 zone, intended for starting dwarves and gnomes. For the quests in Dun Morogh before the Cataclysm, see Dun Morogh (Classic) quests. Encircled by jagged mountain peaks, the snowy region of Dun Morogh has been the cultural heart of Ironforge's dwarves for ages. Not long ago, quakes roused numerous troggs from their subterranean dwellings, and caused the savage Frostmane trolls to abandon their usual holdings on Shimmer Ridge and encroach upon dwarf-occupied areas.

Dun Morogh Sledders are dwarves found on the slopes of Ironforge Mountain in Dun Morogh. They can be seen dragging their sleds up the hill and then riding it down towards New Tinkertown, before crashing in a snow drift and walking back up again. Ollie the pug can be found riding on one of the sleds.

Dun Morogh Chickens are chicken critters that wander just outside of Ironforge in Dun Morogh. One can also be found in Chelie Coldanvil's menagerie of "exotic" creatures at Arbor Glen in Shadowmoon Valley.

Dun Garok Spirits are the ghosts of Riflemen, Priests, Mountaineers and Soldiers who fell proudly in the defense of Dun Garok. Even in death, they still fight for their land. Their former commander Captain Ironhill believes that they have suffered enough and wishes to put them to rest.
Dubenko is the turtle involved in the Darkmoon Faire game Target: Turtle. He has a wooden pole attached to his back and moves erratically around his pen.
The Dull Moonstone Loop is a world drop from level 93 - 97 mobs.
Drupala Nearmiss is a gnome located at the Trueshot Lodge in Highmountain. She is talking with Practicus Rozzbin. She also appeared in Deliverance Point on the Broken Shore.

Dudebrul is a drogbar wandering around the Stonedark Grotto in Highmountain with his right fist up. Adventurers can "fist bump" him to receive the 1-hour "Fist Bumped" buff, the description of which reads: "Fist bumped a brul. Nice."

__NOTOC__ Dug Digger is a Bluewax kobold found in Candle Rock in Highmountain during Candle of Command and Burn the Candle at Both Ends. He claims to be the best digger in Candle Rock, but Intern Jackie says that while he's good enough, he is not the best. During Candle of Command, Dug is the fourth and final kobold to appear to be offered a job by the adventurer. During Burn the Candle at Both Ends, he has been gone for an unusually long amount of time, and so the adventurer is sent to find him. In the southern part of the cave, the champion finds Dug's lifeless body. After checking his pulse to no avail, the adventurer continues on to seek out Kindle Candlecrafter instead.

Drust Archaeology Fragments are found using the Survey ability of the Archaeology skill. As with all Archaeology Fragments, they are not inventory items but instead tracked on the relevant page of a player's archaeology dialog. These fragments are found at Drust archaeology sites.
Du'ba is a Zandalari troll ghost flight master located in Zo'bal Ruins in Nazmir.
__NOTOC__ Duke Szzull is a naga who can be encountered during Island Expeditions.
Dud Blast Canisters have a chance to drop from mobs on Mechagon Island during Ideas Can Come from Anywhere.

The Dumah is a human family located in the Western Plaguelands. Along with the Levine, they once operated the Northridge Lumber Mill. When the Scourge arrived to devastate the land, the mill fell under the control of the Scarlet Crusade. Following the Cataclysm, the son of the mill's owner, Nathaniel Dumah managed to retake it and has now started a new family under the allegiance of the Argent Crusade.

The Duck Cave is an unnamed cave in the Upper Frostlands of the Azure Span. Guarded by a Duck, mages can Blink through the ice wall to gain access. Inside, mages can find Millhouse and Millificent Manastorm, the Manastorming For Beginners tome that begins the quest Best Spell Ever, some more ducks and Mecha Ducks, and Milificent's Teleporter to exit the cave.

Durar's Power Cell drops from Rune-Smith Durar at Dun Argol in the Grizzly Hills.
Duskingdawn's Wand is provided as an objective for A Fighting Chance. Despite the description, it is used to empower Hill Fawns with fel energy.

The Dunwald Ruins, located in the southwestern-central part of the Twilight Highlands, are what remains of the Dunwald clan home. Led by the ettin Darunga, the Twilight's Hammer attacked and sacked the town, killing many of its citizens. Only a handful of them survived. It contains Dunwald Holdout, Dunwald Town Square, and Dunwald Market Row, but not Dunwald Hovel. The ale stores were in a building near the old well, but the Hammer destroyed them as well. It also has a smithy in the market row.

The Dunwald clan, or Clan Dunwald, is a small clan of Wildhammer dwarves located in the Dunwald Ruins. They seem to be excellent warriors as four of them had no difficulty in killing the ettin responsible for destroying their town. There are few things in the highlands as terrifying as the Dunwalds reunited. Donnelly is the eldest of the Dunwalds. Cayden and Eoin are the twins.

Durable Worghide Cape is a cloak geared towards melee classes. Absence of any primary stats (such as agility, strength and stamina) is particularly notable. Because of that, this cloak is useful to a wider range of players as is usually the case with these gear pieces.

Durak is an orc warlock and quest giver in the back of the Splintertree Mine in Ashenvale. Both Kadrak and Draaka request his services to defend Splintertree Post against the night elf assault, but Draaka later regrets her usage of fel magic and sends the adventurer to Orgrimmar to inform Eitrigg of her crime. In response, Eitrigg sends the adventurer back to Splintertree to tell Durak that the Horde will have nothing to do with his kind. When told of this, Durak says that "this is all happening sooner than I would like" and that the adventurer has outgrown their usefulness before revealing his true form: a demonic terrorguard.

Durin Darkhammer is a Dark Iron dwarf master Pet Tamer located south of Blackrock Mountain in Burning Steppes. He is surrounded by his three level 17 battle pets: Comet, Ignious, and Moltar. Defeating him is required to complete the Taming Eastern Kingdoms achievement.
Durable Necklace of the Golden Lotus is a quest reward from The Final Power.
Durphorn the Bullheaded is a tauren fighting Iron Horde Grunts alongside many others at the Dark Portal in Blasted Lands and Tanaan Jungle. He died after the portal was destroyed.
Durotan's Grasp is a small camp west of in Talador. This location has a flight path and a vendor, but nothing else.

]] The dusk lily is a species of flower native to the region of Suramar on the Broken Isles. The plant is characterized by petals of watermelon pink with dark green serrated leaves. The image of the dusk lily came to prominence at the time of the Nightfallen rebellion in Suramar City, where it was symbolically associated with the rebellion's leader, First Arcanist Thalyssra, and grew to represent the entire movement. Following the victory of the Nightfallen in the civil war against Grand Magistrix Elisande, and the subsequent creation of a new government in Suramar, the dusk lily became the insignia of the nightborne race.
Durotan's Pride is a destroyer located at the Frostwall Shipyard in Frostfire Ridge.
Dungeon Delver is a passive racial ability for all Dark Iron dwarves, increasing movement speed while indoors.

Dusklight Matriarch is a razorwing hovering above the Razorwing Nest on the western edge of the Windswept Aerie in Korthia. She is looking for the Lost Razorwing Egg. Duskcoat Den-Mothers are tigers located in Island Expeditions.
Dusk-Crusher Handguards drop from the Sisters of the Moon in the Tomb of Sargeras.
Duskwalker's Patch is a runecarving power obtained from Memory of the Duskwalker's Patch.

Duskwood, originally called Brightwood, is a fiefdom of the Kingdom of Stormwind located in the southern-central part of Azeroth, south of Elwynn Forest, east of Westfall, west of Deadwind Pass, and north of Stranglethorn Vale. Beneath the everlasting night, which gave Duskwood its current name, the fel magic unleashed by Medivh upon his death has transformed what was once a beautiful part of Elwynn Forest into a land covered in gnarled trees, along with the black fog hanging over the woods. Duskwood is inhabited by a defiant people who still cling to their holdings in the face of overwhelming adversity. On all sides lurk dangerous creatures, from hideous undead to ferocious Nightbane worgen

Dustwallow Bay is a portion of the Great Sea off the eastern coast of central Kalimdor, mostly noted by travelers on the eastern coast of the Dustwallow Marsh west of Theramore Isle. Nat Pagle the noted fisherman is located on an island just off the bay in Tidefury Cove.

Dustfire Valley is a windswept valley in the Searing Gorge that leads north to the locked gates of Stonewrought Pass to the Valley of Kings in Loch Modan. Though the gates are locked, it is possible through a quest chain to obtain a key. For most travelers, however, it is easier to fly into the gorge.
The Dwarven Fishing Pole was a quest reward from Murloc Poachers which started with Dockmaster Baren at Lakeshire in Redridge Mountains.
Duskwither Apprentices are Wretched who live in the Duskwither Spire in Eversong Woods and guard the Duskwither power sources.

is the Warcraft III rifleman art.]] A dwarf sharphooter is an Ironforge dwarf warrior. Ironforge dwarves have a strong tradition of firearm proficiency. In particular, they focus on the long rifle and the blunderbuss. Dwarven riflemen were valuable assets in the Third War, able to pick off vulnerable and important targets from behind their own lines. Honed senses allow these skilled dwarves to detect when their equipment is about to break down on them, and they have a certain ability to quickly clear a jam so they can get back to fightin'.
Dusky is a nightsaber located in Aldor Rise in Shattrath City, acoompanying Caylee Dak.
The Dusty Journal is a book located on the top floor of Dawnstar Spire in Ghostlands.
The three Duskwither Spire Power Sources are located in Duskwither Spire of Eversong Woods.

Duun was an orc warrior who fought alongside Broxigar to hold a mountain pass against the Burning Legion during the Battle of Mount Hyjal. He was beheaded by a demon, his head bouncing along the ground several seconds before his torso collapsed.
Dust Cloud is one of the pet abilities that only tallstriders can use.
Dwarfageddon (10 player) was a dungeon & raids achievement earned for destroying 100 Steelforged Defenders in 10 seconds on the Ulduar gauntlet on 10-player mode.

Dustwind Dig is situated in the hills above Hammertoe's Digsite in the Badlands and is the expanded Alliance camp of Sigrun Ironhew. It contains a flight path. Following the Fourth War, the Explorers' League is still present and active on the digsite in the region.

Dwarf Archaeology Fragments are found using the Survey ability of the Archaeology skill. As with all Archaeology Fragments, they are not inventory items but instead tracked on the relevant page of a player's archaeology dialog. These fragments are found at Dwarven archaeology sites.

The Duskwood storyline takes place after the Redridge Mountains storyline for level 20-25 Alliance players, typically humans. It begins in Darkshire and proceeds to the crossroads between Westfall and Northern Stranglethorn where Apprentice Fess waits. From there the quests progress to the newly upgraded Raven Hill. Completing these quests grants the achievement Duskwood Quests. After Duskwood comes the Northern Stranglethorn storyline.

The Dwarven Scouts were a group of scouts led by Muradin Bronzebeard, who ended being cut off from the main Dwarven Expedition by the Undead Scourge. The scouting was eventually aided by Prince Arthas and his forces and was soon after reunited with the main expedition after destroying the undead base blocking them.

The Dwarven Expedition was an Explorers' League force led by Muradin Bronzebeard in order to explore the continent of Northrend and find the runeblade Frostmourne. As the expedition ventured deeper into Northrend they found more and more undead and the Undead Scourge was eventually able to separate the expedition from its leader (who had gone on a scouting mission) and trap them. Eventually the sudden arrival of Prince Arthas and his forces would help free the expedition from the undead and with Muradin back in command the expedition would aid the 1st Legion against the undead. Dustwallow Marsh is a level 35-40 zone in Central Kalimdor. Both the Alliance and the Horde have a presence here, at the human port city of Theramore Isle and the ogre-populated Brackenwall Village, respectively. In addition, goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel have set up the town of Mudsprocket to the southwest. The progress of the storyline is tracked in the achievement Dustwallow Marsh Quests.
